1.why: All screens are static, card-based layouts with no animations or pop-ups, though the persistent monospace Logs/token panel adds some visual clutter below every form.

2.why: Bold headings and high-contrast blue primary buttons make the main actions stand out, but on the privacy-conditions screen the checkbox is oddly centered and separated from its split label, weakening that key control.

3.why: Each screen presents a single labeled task with one primary button, but finding the required codes means scrolling to the Logs panel and transcribing a 40-character token.

4.why: The flow demands many sequential steps (email, long recovery token, second MFA code, a password meeting five rules, sign-in, acceptance), although each rule is displayed on screen rather than requiring memorization.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, autofill hint, or password-manager affordance is visible on any sign-in or password screen.

6.why: All fields are blank with no saved or prefilled items (e.g., the sign-in email is empty even after the reset flow), so there is nothing familiar to recognize.

7.why: Instructions are short and plain ('Enter your account email address', 'Your password must have at least 12 characters...'), with only minor jargon in the Logs panel ('SIMULATED MFA DELIVERY').

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the ten screenshots, so whether error messages describe the problem and fix cannot be verified.

9.why: Input fields have no placeholder examples (no sample email or example password format), so the user is not shown what to type.

10.why: The system offers no login choices at all—only password sign-in with one code-based recovery path—and no face login or alternative method is presented.

11.why: Every screen presents exactly one decision and one primary button (send, verify, confirm, save, accept, sign out), so choices are never stacked.

12.why: Dedicated outcome screens confirm each action, e.g., 'Password updated — your recovery code is no longer valid' and 'Privacy conditions accepted — your authenticated session has recorded your acceptance.'

13.why: Each new step carries a short guiding instruction and a persistent 'Keep your account safe' tip, though there is no dedicated help link or contextual help icon.

14.why: Recovery options exist for mistakes: 'Request another code', 'Forgot password?', and 'Return to sign in' links allow restarting steps.

15.why: Header, card structure, button styling, safety banner, and Logs panel are identical across all ten steps, with only the misaligned privacy-checkbox row breaking visual consistency.
